Subject: So this happened. Fernhollow Photo is officially a thing!!

Quick update from the trenches, except this time the trenches are apparently MY BUSINESS. Fernhollow Photo is real!! Like, registered LLC, actual website, actual couples trusting me to show up at their weddings real. I'm going out on my own as a wedding photographer. I have typed that sentence about six times and it still looks a little nuts.

I wanted to tell you all before Thanksgiving because I would rather eat Aunt Ruthie's turkey than try to make a big announcement while somebody is asking me to pass the gravy. Also I would like a minute to be excited with everybody. This is a big, good thing, and I'm really proud of it, even if saying that makes me want to hide behind my camera.

First, the work news. Rosebud Lane closed at the end of October. Marisol told me on October 6, and after four years shooting for her, knowing that chapter was ending was a lot. Four years is a lot of weddings, a lot of loading gear into cars, a lot of trying to figure out where the groom's brother wandered off to when we specifically said EVERYBODY STAY HERE.

Marisol basically taught me everything. Not just how to get the picture, but how to take care of people on a day when they have approximately nine thousand feelings and haven't eaten since breakfast. How to pay attention. How to keep moving when the schedule has become more of a suggestion. I'm so grateful I got to work with her, and whatever Fernhollow becomes, there's going to be a whole lot of what she taught me in it.

She's also already referred six of her 2027 couples to me. That kind of trust means more than I can really explain without getting weepy, so we're going to keep moving.

Here's the part I keep looking at to make sure I didn't make it up: I already have 14 weddings booked for 2027. Six came through Marisol, and eight found me on my own. Fourteen!! June is going to be a situation. There are four weddings that month, so if I show up somewhere wearing two different socks, just let it happen.

The first booking that felt completely mine was Dahlia and Ken. June 12 at Timberline. They found me through the photos I took of a Rosebud Lane couple at Multnomah Falls, and they wanted ME. Not just an available photographer. Me, because they liked the pictures I made. I know that's sort of the whole idea of this business, but when it actually happens it turns out you lose the ability to act normal for a bit.

Their deposit came in and I was like, oh. Ok. We're doing this.

And before Dad gets to the comments: YES, I have health insurance sorted. I picked a marketplace plan, and it starts January 1. January 1, Dad. You can still ask me about it because I know you love me, but ideally we can do that without making it the main event at Thanksgiving. I would like the main event to remain stuffing.

I'm scared, obviously. I'm excited enough that I keep interrupting myself with new things to be scared about. But this isn't something I thought up last Tuesday because I liked a font. I've been planning this in my head for two years. The timing got very real very fast, but wanting to do it didn't come out of nowhere.

I've worked through the numbers, I've got bookings on the calendar, and I'm not planning to do every single thing alone. Jae will second shoot the bigger weddings with me, paid per wedding. Having another photographer there for those days matters. I can move pretty fast, but I still can't be in two rooms at once, despite several wedding timelines suggesting otherwise.

The LLC paperwork happened on October 22, on my lunch break, sitting in the car outside a Fred Meyer. Which is exactly the glamorous business origin story you would expect from me. I filed it and cried a little. Just sitting there in a parking lot being a person who apparently owns a company now. Then lunch break was over. Very rude of time to continue normally.

The website went live November 1. Sam made a cake that said FERNHOLOW. One L short, full points for cake. We ate it anyway. I feel like if your business hasn't even really started yet and somebody has already made you a slightly misspelled celebration cake, you're doing pretty well.

And Grandma, I need you to know where the name came from.

It's for the fern hollow trail behind your old place in Gresham. Where I took my first real pictures with your Pentax. I kept coming back to that when I was trying to figure out what to call this, because before there were wedding schedules or contracts or any of this, there was me with your camera, figuring out that I really, really liked taking pictures.

So Fernhollow is for you. I wanted that little piece of where I started to come with me. Now I'm getting weepy again. Very professional update we're having here.

Anyway. That's my news. I'm a business owner, my knees are still the same knees, and I am really excited to see what I can make of this. You don't have to pretend it isn't scary. I know it is. But I have a plan, and four years of doing this work, and people who want me to photograph their weddings. That's a pretty good place to start.

Also, does anybody want free family pictures at Thanksgiving? I'll bring the camera. We can do a few before dinner while there's light and before we all become physically incapable of leaving the couch. Tell me if you're interested so we can wrangle people. Uncle Greg, I cannot promise it won't be cold. I can promise to try to be quick.

Mom, yes, Sam is coming. We're bringing rolls and the cranberry thing.

Love you all. Please be excited with me!! And Grandma, yes, I want a picture with you.
